ov: Fifteen species of large birds with long legs and necks, often called the world’s tallest flying birds. Most are grey or white with red bare skin on the face; crowned cranes have golden crests. They fly with the neck stretched out, unlike herons.
wt: Up to 12 kg (red-crowned crane, the heaviest)
rg: Every continent except Antarctica and South America.
df: Opportunistic: small rodents, birds’ eggs, fish, amphibians, insects, grain and berries.

cf.tip: A crane flies with its neck stretched out; a heron pulls its neck back into an S.

fx: Both parents raise the chicks, which stay with them until the next breeding season.
The plight of North America’s whooping crane inspired some of the first US laws protecting endangered species.
